chunks: O mankind, a parable has been presented, so listen to it. Those you call upon other than Allah will never create a fly, even if they gather together to do so; and if the fly were to steal something from them, they would not be able to retrieve it from it. Weak is the seeker and weak is the sought.
ai.seo_question: What is the meaning of the parable of the fly in Surah Al-Hajj?
ai.summary: In Surah Al-Hajj, this verse employs a striking rhetorical device by contrasting the collective impotence of idols with the singular weakness of a fly, emphasizing that both the worshippers (the weak claimants) and the worshipped (the weak idols) are equally powerless. Shia exegetes, such as Al-Tabarsi in *Majma' al-Bayan*, highlight this as a definitive proof of Tawhid, illustrating that if false gods cannot even create or retrieve a tiny creature, they are utterly incapable of granting benefit or averting harm. This metaphor serves as a practical reminder for believers to direct their supplications solely to the All-Powerful Creator.
